correctness.rationale: Exact discrepancy update d_i = Q(L_i-P_i) and equivalence d_i<=Q to unit-chore Prop1 are verified. For n<=3 a hand-readable eight-state complete transition table and singleton neutrality prove indefinite greedy feasibility. For n=4 the four-level exhaustive greedy recurrence includes all nonsingleton eligibility sets and all tied greedy recipients, yielding state counts (1,28,187,617,1405) with maximum d_i<=12. An explicit full-branch five-chore adaptive tree forces d_i>12, independently confirmed by exact minimax. For n>=5 two universal jobs and a pair job force violation, with the <3 lower bound proved for all n. The checker extracted from the final package was run successfully; bounded computations do not replace the all-horizon invariant or the algebraic all-n argument.

originality.rationale: The first-public 2026 eligibility-aware online proportionality paper supplies asymptotic approximation bounds, not the exact all-horizon three-agent positive frontier and exceptional four-agent five-job horizon. Its general many-agent lower-bound idea explains, but is not claimed as originality for, the easy n>=5 three-job case. The earlier relevance-orientation paper is offline. Public literature searches, targeted research-record searches, and recoverable neighboring mathematical claims did not identify a statement implying the all-horizon n<=3 guarantee together with the four-agent minimal horizon. Absolute historical priority remains uncertain.

value.rationale: The motivating 2026 work determines only asymptotic online Prop1 approximability under restricted assignment; the exact smallest machine count permitting impossibility and the exceptional first-failure length at four machines are natural structural boundaries. Proving indefinite feasibility for three machines and a shortest five-job obstruction for four separates long-term online solvability from finite-horizon adversarial failure. The precise four-agent threshold is neither an arbitrary slice nor a numerical refinement of a known table: it identifies the last exceptional regime before the elementary three-job many-agent adversary works.
